title: Zero-downtime listener handoff: five mechanisms, one invariant
summary: Mechanisms: (a) fd inheritance via exec (nginx NGINX env, tableflip, shellflip), (b) SCM_RIGHTS over a UDS (HAProxy -x, Envoy hot restart, Pingora --upgrade, Proxygen Socket Takeover), (c) systemd socket unit / fd store holding the socket outside the process, (d) bind-with-SO_REUSEPORT in a second process (loses queued conns, rejected by Cloudflare/HAProxy), (e) kernel socket migration (tcp_migrate_req + BPF select) or BPF-steered REUSEPORT groups (nginx quic_bpf). The only mechanism class with zero queue loss by construction is one where the same kernel socket object (same accept queue) stays open throughout: (a)(b)(c).
overclaim_risk: Not every mechanism was benchmarked by us; loss rates are vendor/blog-reported.
underclaim_risk: Kernel socket migration (5.14+) narrows the gap for SO_REUSEPORT designs; do not dismiss it.

title: Same-socket handoff beats SO_REUSEPORT-second-process for accept-queue integrity; REUSEPORT needs explicit claim/close discipline
summary: A second process binding with SO_REUSEPORT creates a separate kernel socket with its own accept queue; closing the old one resets queued connections (HAProxy measured 2-3 resets per million connections per reload; 155 per million after 180 reloads at 55k conn/s, 10 reloads/s, kernel 4.9). Passing the existing fd keeps the queue (HAProxy ab test: restart 11/2000 failed, plain reload 1, fd transfer 0). With REUSEPORT groups passed by fd, every received fd MUST be claimed or closed or it black-holes its share (Proxygen paper; Pingora close_unclaimed). Envoy: decreasing worker concurrency across a hot restart can drop accept-queue connections.
overclaim_risk: Loss numbers are from 2017 kernel 4.9 and a vendor blog (HAProxy Tech), small samples.
underclaim_risk: Modern kernels with tcp_migrate_req may reduce this; no independent measurement found.

title: HAProxy seamless reload (fd transfer over CLI socket), 1.8 (2017)
summary: New process connects to old process's stats/CLI unix socket (requires bind option expose-fd listeners; reload with -x <sock> -sf <pid>); old sends listener fds with SCM_RIGHTS; max 253 listeners in the 2017 design. Source: src/cli.c _getsocks sends MAX_SEND_FD fds per sendmsg, expose-fd only accepts 'listeners' (ACCESS_FD_LISTENERS). Extends gap.haproxy.

title: nginx binary upgrade (USR2/WINCH/QUIT) and reload (HUP)
summary: USR2: master renames pidfile to .oldbin, execs new binary with env NGINX="fd;fd;..." (ngx_exec_new_binary in src/core/nginx.c builds it from cycle->listening; ngx_add_inherited_sockets getenv-parses it). Old master keeps listen sockets so it can spawn workers on rollback (HUP to old, QUIT to new). WINCH drains old workers; QUIT old commits. Mixed old/new workers both accept during overlap. Reload (HUP) keeps same master and listening sockets, closes only idle keepalive.

title: Envoy hot restart: UDS datagram RPC, new process initializes first, then requests listeners
summary: Child fully initializes (config, initial discovery, health checks) before asking the parent for listen sockets (pass_listen_socket by worker index for reuse_port sockets); parent then drained (--drain-time-s) and shut down (--parent-shutdown-time-s, should exceed drain). Counters/gauges transferred; connections are NOT. Source: source/server/hot_restarting_{base,parent,child}.cc; AF_UNIX SOCK_DGRAM at <socket_path>_<role>_<base_id+id>, fchmod(socket_mode); one SCM_RIGHTS fd per message. Extends gap.envoy.

title: Pingora graceful upgrade: --upgrade + upgrade socket + SIGQUIT; source-level hardening evidence
summary: New instance started with --upgrade requests listeners over a configured UDS; SIGQUIT to old triggers transfer then graceful shutdown. pingora-core/src/server/transfer_fd/mod.rs (737 lines): MAX_FDS=32 per recvmsg, MAX_RETRY=5 at 1s, nonblocking send polls 20x500ms; recvmsg uses MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC with an in-code rationale (subprocess exec'd by app would otherwise keep the port bound after server exit); close_unclaimed() closes inherited SO_REUSEPORT fds absent from the new config because 'an unclaimed SO_REUSEPORT socket ... can black-hole connections'; tests assert FD_CLOEXEC and no fd leak. Extends gap.pingora and w02.pingora-tokio-panic context.
overclaim_risk: Docs describe no guarantee for in-flight connections beyond grace period; do not read 'no connection refused' as 'no connection dropped'.

title: Facebook Zero Downtime Release (SIGCOMM 2020): Socket Takeover, Downstream Connection Reuse, Partial Post Replay
summary: Naseer, Niccolini, Pant, Frindell, Dasineni, Benson; doi 10.1145/3387514.3405885, pp 529-541. Socket Takeover passes all listening FDs (TCP and UDP VIPs) via SCM_RIGHTS; for QUIC/UDP the new process user-space-routes packets of pre-existing flows to the old process by connection ID during drain. Edge L7 drain 20 min; app servers 10-15 s; release time 25 min (app tier) and 90 min (L7LB); +15-20% effective L7LB CPU capacity; takeover costs <1% idle CPU (parallel process); binary updates ~47% of releases; hard restart of 10% of Origin proxies made the app cluster spend 20% of CPU rebuilding state; PPR uses HTTP 379 to replay partial POSTs to another server.
overclaim_risk: Hyperscaler scale and a Katran L4 tier it relies on; not directly transferable to a single VPS.
underclaim_risk: The failure-mode section (orphan sockets, fd leaks, kernel GSO bug surviving restarts) is the most transferable content.

title: systemd file descriptor store + socket units for the single-node household upgrade
summary: FileDescriptorStoreMax= (default 0=off); service pushes fds with sd_pid_notify_with_fds FDSTORE=1 (+FDNAME, FDPOLL=0 to avoid auto-removal on POLLHUP/ERR); returned at next start through LISTEN_FDS/LISTEN_FDNAMES/LISTEN_PID/LISTEN_PIDFDID; FDSTOREREMOVE=1 required when the service closes its copy; store kept across a restart job but cleared on full stop unless FileDescriptorStorePreserve=yes|on-success; NotifyAccess= restricts who may modify (default main PID only; =all for child processes); systemd-analyze fdstore lists. kexec/LUO preserves memfd only (sockets dropped). systemd.socket: Accept=no passes sockets to one service; Backlog= default 4294967295 silently capped by net.core.somaxconn (usually 4096); FlushPending=no keeps pending conns for restarted service; ReusePort= option exists. A restart via fdstore keeps listener queue but kills accepted connections of the old process: it gives zero-refusal, not zero-drop.
overclaim_risk: Cannot by itself preserve accepted connections.
underclaim_risk: Combined with an in-process child-spawn handover (shellflip-style) it covers both queue and accepted connections on one node.

title: Caddy config reload: graph-swap via admin API, drain-or-grace_period semantics
summary: caddy reload = POST /load; failed config keeps old config running; identical config skipped unless --force; reload call blocks until requests on old config finish, long-lived WebSocket/SSE/downloads stall it unless the global grace_period option cancels them. Not a binary upgrade (same process), so no fd handoff and no binary swap. STEK: modules/caddytls/sessiontickets.go RotationInterval default 12h, MaxKeys default 4, 32-byte keys; distributed_stek (storage-coordinated) for clusters. Extends gap.caddy.
overclaim_risk: Reload semantics taken from community answers plus source; official doc page not fetched.

title: Kernel SO_REUSEPORT socket migration (tcp_migrate_req) and its 2026 bug
summary: Iwashima 11-patch series (v8 2021-06, LKML) adds net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req and BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE: on close()/shutdown() of a listener, queued established and SYN_RECV children migrate to a sibling listener in the same reuseport group; without a BPF program kernel picks a random live listener; mismatched socket options (e.g. TCP_SAVE_SYN) can crash apps. CVE-2026-46015 (published 2026-05-27, modified 2026-10-19, CVSS3.1 7.8 per INCIBE page): sk_data_ready() not called after migration in inet_csk_listen_stop, so epoll/accept waiters on the target listener can sleep forever; affected ranges 5.14..<5.15.209, 5.16..<6.1.175, 6.2..<6.6.140, 6.7..<6.12.86, 6.13..<6.18.27, 6.19..<7.0.4. Implication: a kernel-migration-based design must pin kernels >= those fixes and add an accept-liveness watchdog.
overclaim_risk: CVE data from a single aggregator page (not cross-checked against NVD/kernel.org); sysctl default and 5.14 mainline version from search snippet.

title: Orphan fd failure modes: black-holed REUSEPORT sockets and leaked sockets surviving process death
summary: Proxygen paper section 5.1: (i) if the new process ignores a received SO_REUSEPORT fd without closing or listening, the kernel keeps routing its share of packets/connections there and they idle until timeout; (ii) a passed fd is equivalent to dup(), so leaked fds keep the socket (and its buffers) alive after the process terminates; a UDP GSO kernel bug accumulated buffers and a process restart did not clear it because the socket object persisted. Remediations in paper: explicit ready acknowledgement before old process drains, dynamic disable switch for takeover, version-compat of the takeover protocol, Katran LRU connection-table cache. Independent corroboration: Pingora close_unclaimed + MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC comments (2026 tree).

title: HTTP/2 graceful drain = two GOAWAYs (RFC 9113 s6.8); what drops vs what is retried
summary: Server SHOULD send initial GOAWAY with last_stream_id=2^31-1 and NO_ERROR, wait >= 1 RTT for in-flight stream creation, then send a second GOAWAY with the real last stream id; endpoints MUST NOT increase last_stream_id; streams above it were not processed and are safely retriable; a client unable to retry (e.g. intermediary serving non-H2 clients) loses in-flight requests. Fetched from rfc-editor.org 2026-10-25. Implication: drain deadline D must exceed longest tolerated request; requests/streams crossing D are lost unless the app supports Proxygen-style partial replay.

title: QUIC across restarts: CID routing is the only way; nginx quic_bpf, Proxygen user-space forwarding, QUIC-LB draft
summary: UDP has no accept queue: during a handover the 4-tuple hash can send packets of an old connection to the new process, which has no state. Proxygen forwards by connection ID in user space to the old process. nginx quic_bpf (Linux 5.7+; since 1.31.7 per docs fetched 2026-10-25) uses eBPF CID routing to keep established QUIC connections across reload and live upgrade; cannot be toggled on reload; quic_host_key default regenerated per reload so old Retry/stateless-reset tokens are rejected. IETF draft-ietf-quic-load-balancers-22 (2026-10-23, expires 2027-04-26): server ID in CID (3-bit config rotation, AES-ECB single-pass or 4-round Feistel), sec 6.4 non-normative process demux. Decision: AEGIS H3 can ship with 'connection loss on upgrade, clients reconnect via 0-RTT/new CID' unless CID-routing is implemented.
overclaim_risk: nginx 1.31.7 version number taken from the doc page; not verified in release notes.

title: STEK continuity across reload/upgrade/scale-out: lifetimes in the wild and in code
summary: Springall/Durumeric/Halderman IMC 2016 (Alexa top-1M, 9-week scan): 354,697 domains issued tickets; 38% of sites decryptable >24h after a server compromise and 10% >30 days; STEK reuse: 41% daily-unique, 22% >=7 days, 10% (28,210) >=30 days; 12 Alexa-top-100 sites reused >=30 days. Implementation facts: nginx auto-rotated keys live in the ssl_session_cache shared zone (3 slots, RAND_bytes(80), expire=now+session timeout; since 1.23.2) else random-per-start unless ssl_session_ticket_key files (first encrypts, rest decrypt-only); Caddy 12h rotation, 4 keys max (so worst-case key life ~48h); Cloudflare (2015) hourly random keys from in-memory daemon, kept 18h, never on disk; rustls TicketRotator: ticketer valid for >=1 and <=2 lifetimes. Inference (unverified): nginx binary upgrade creates a fresh shm zone so tickets from the old master stop resuming; our design should pass the ring explicitly.
overclaim_risk: 2016 data; TLS1.3 tickets are PSK-based so forward secrecy is lost differently; do not quote percentages as current.
underclaim_risk: Cross-vhost ticket scoping is already a separate map node (crs-ce-tls-ticket-cross-vhost).

title: Cloudflare 2025-11-18: globally pushed auto-generated config exceeded proxy limit, Rust unwrap panic
summary: 11:20-14:30 UTC main impact (~3h10), full resolution 17:06 (5h46 total). A ClickHouse permissions change doubled the Bot Management feature file (limit 200 features, ~60 used); FL2 proxy panicked on Result::unwrap(); file regenerated every 5 min and pushed network-wide giving flapping good/bad states; fix: stop propagation, manually insert known-good file, force core proxy restart. Remediations: treat internally generated config like user input, add global kill switches. Lesson for AEGIS: reload path must (1) validate+parse in a staging context before swap, (2) keep last-known-good on any error (Caddy semantic), (3) never panic on config ingest, (4) canary the push.

title: Drain-forever failure: old workers linger with long-lived connections (HAProxy, nginx, Caddy, Envoy)
summary: HAProxy soft-stop old workers live until last connection closes; mitigations hard-stop-after (since 1.7.4), reload-storm leaks of fds and memory documented on Discourse/GitLab (community grade); nginx 2017-09 thread: limit_conn drops/memory growth with frequent reloads, old workers up to 30 min; Red Hat bz1320233 OpenShift router reload per endpoint resync dropping connections (fix: <=1 reload per sync); Caddy reload blocks on WebSocket/SSE until grace_period; Envoy needs --drain-time-s < --parent-shutdown-time-s. Implication: every drain needs a hard deadline, a metric for old-generation connection count, and rate-limited reloads (coalesce).
overclaim_risk: Mostly forum/vendor-blog evidence; no dated formal postmortem of a reload-induced outage at a named company found except Cloudflare 2025 config push (different mechanism).

title: Reload as attack surface: env-var fd injection, unauthenticated handoff socket, fd leaks, privilege at re-exec
summary: (1) nginx NGINX env var is trusted: any party able to set the env of the exec'd binary can make nginx adopt arbitrary inherited fd numbers as listeners (src/core/nginx.c ngx_add_inherited_sockets; no type/addr verification before ngx_set_inherited_sockets). (2) Envoy hot-restart IPC is an unauthenticated AF_UNIX datagram socket protected only by filesystem mode; RELEASE_ASSERT aborts on unexpected cmsg; GitHub issue envoyproxy/envoy#45872 (2026-06-29, OPEN, reporter-assigned CVSS 6.1 AV:L) wire-length+8 overflow -> resize(0) -> heap overflow; main already carries a guard dropping datagrams with length > UINT64_MAX-8. (3) HAProxy expose-fd listeners grants fd-extraction to anyone with access to that CLI socket level. (4) leaked listener fds into children keep ports bound after exit (Pingora MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC comment). (5) a new binary is code execution with the old process's privileges: path must be pinned and hash/signature-verified. Mitigations for AEGIS: handover socket created by supervisor with SO_PEERCRED uid+pid check, abstract-free path under 0700 dir, validate each received fd (SO_TYPE, SO_ACCEPTCONN, getsockname == configured bind), strict length caps, no panics (return error), ASLR-independent; fuzz the handover parser.
overclaim_risk: Envoy #45872 is an unconfirmed reporter claim (AV:L, needs local socket write); nginx env injection requires pre-existing control of the exec environment (not a remote vector).

title: Rust fd-passing and socket-activation crates, status as of 2026-10-25 (crates.io API)
summary: listenfd 1.0.2 (2025-01-19; 6.9M dl); sd-notify 0.5.0 (2026-03-09; 16.4M dl; has notify_with_fds, NotifyState::FdStore/FdStoreRemove, listen_fds_with_names); sd-listen-fds 0.2.0 (2023-08-27; 130k dl; Ralith); passfd 0.1.6 (2023-02-24; 572k); sendfd 0.4.5 (2026-09-26; 16.8M dl; standard-ai); nix 0.31.3 (2026-05-11; 906M dl; recvmsg + MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC + cmsg_space!); libsystemd 0.7.2 (2025-04-30); shellflip 2.1.3 (2026-10-14; 1.42M dl; Cloudflare; BSD) = tableflip-style restarts; tokio-unix-ipc 0.4.0 (2025-02-23); listen_fds 0.1.0 (2026-03-03; 165 dl). No crates.io crate named tableflip. unsafe LOC / audit status of each not measured (spike).
overclaim_risk: Download counts are not quality; none were audited for unsafe/soundness.
underclaim_risk: nix + sd-notify alone suffice to implement the whole protocol with no custom unsafe.

title: shellflip handover internals (source read): two pipes + inherited coordination UDS, no parent timeout
summary: Handover state through pipe fd in OXY_HANDOVER_PIPE, readiness via completion pipe fd in OXY_NOTIFY_SOCKET, restart coordination via inherited listening UDS OXY_RESTART_SOCKET (clear_cloexec in pre_exec); LISTEN_PID='auto' then fixed up for systemd; child calls sd_notify READY; parent kills child on failure; 3 unsafe blocks; spawning on a dedicated thread to survive seccomp on main thread. Parent wait on completion pipe has no timeout (a hung but alive child blocks upgrade). Does not itself pass listener fds in the shown code: app must put listeners in handover state.
overclaim_risk: Read via a fetch summarizer, not full local read of the repository; other modules (pipes) not inspected.

title: Horizontal scale-out: what state must be shared and the option per state
summary: STEK: (a) per-node random keys (resumption only on same node; zero coordination), (b) shared ring from storage (Caddy distributed_stek; Cloudflare in-memory daemon + replication; nginx ssl_session_ticket_key files), (c) derive epoch keys from a shared master secret by HKDF(master, epoch) [design option, no cited production example]. Rate limit: local-only (Envoy local limit multiplies by replica count), per-site consistent-hash counters (Cloudflare Twemproxy), gossip aggregation (Raghavan 2007), Redis atomic Lua (centralized). Idempotency keys: need a linearizable create-if-absent keyed by (client,key) with 409/422 semantics (IETF draft -08 says nothing on multi-node): single-owner by consistent hashing of key, or DB unique constraint. Sessions: stateless sealed tokens vs shared store. Audit log: one sequencer per log (Tessera assigns contiguous durable indices per batch, order within batch unspecified, checkpoint needs witness cosignatures) so multi-node means one log per node or a single sequencing service. Extends abuse-rate-limit-algos-crates, sdg-idempotency-draft, ops.audit-log-spec, crs-ce-stek-lifecycle.
overclaim_risk: Option (c) HKDF-epoch STEK is our own sketch, unproven in production.
underclaim_risk: Single-node household case needs none of this; scale-out can be deferred behind a trait boundary.

title: Measured costs of distributed counters (only two primary datapoints found)
summary: Cloudflare 2017: sliding-window approximation rate = prev*(W-elapsed)/W + cur; on 400M requests from 270,000 sources 0.003% wrong decisions, 6% mean rate deviation, 0 false positives, 3 false-allowed sources all <15% over threshold; 2 numbers per counter; async increments; per-PoP only (anycast keeps a client in one PoP), several billion requests/day. Raghavan et al. SIGCOMM 2007: gossip branching factor 3 costs 48 B x 20/s x 3 = 2.88 kbps per limiter, 1.4 Mbps total at 490 limiters = <3% overhead relative to global limit; benefit plateaus past branching factor 3; matched a centralized token bucket on long-term throughput in low-loss TCP tests. No measured Redis-vs-gossip latency comparison found (blog claims ~1 ms Redis call are grade E).
overclaim_risk: Both are old (2007, 2017) and traffic/bandwidth, not request-cost, limits.

title: Proxygen release numbers (for BENCH_PLAN honesty)
summary: Release time 25 min app tier / 90 min L7LB; effective L7LB CPU +15-20%; 20% batch hard restart drops cluster to <85% capacity; takeover <1% idle CPU; Partial Post Replay median disrupted-connection fraction 0.0008 (percent unit per figure, billions of POSTs/min); packet misrouting during takeover without CID routing is visible in Fig. 10. Use as order-of-magnitude, not target.
overclaim_risk: Figures read via pdftotext of a two-column layout; Fig. 11 unit ambiguity.

title: L5: AEGIS in-place upgrade protocol (single node, systemd) with invariants UP-1..UP-7
summary: Actors: S=systemd (Type=notify, FileDescriptorStoreMax=64, NotifyAccess=all, FileDescriptorStorePreserve=yes), A=serving process, B=new binary. Steps: (0) A holds flock(/run/aegis/upgrade.lock) -> one upgrade at a time. (1) `aegisctl upgrade <path>`: control socket (0700 dir, SO_PEERCRED uid==service uid) ; A verifies B's sha256+signature against pinned release key; runs `B --check-config` (parse+validate, no bind). (2) A spawns B on a dedicated pre-seccomp thread with listener fds (CLOEXEC cleared only in pre_exec), handover pipe (carries: STEK ring with ids+ages, generation counter, rate-limit snapshot optional), completion pipe; LISTEN_PID rewritten. (3) B validates every inherited fd (SO_TYPE, SO_ACCEPTCONN, getsockname == config bind), claims or closes the rest, starts accept loops, writes ACCEPTING; (4) A on ACCEPTING sends sd_notify MAINPID=<B>, pushes FDSTORE=1 for B's fds (or B does), stops its own accept loops (does NOT close listener fds until B ACK_OWNS), sends H2 GOAWAY(2^31-1) -> >=1 RTT -> GOAWAY(last), starts drain with deadline D (default 30 s, hard max configurable); (5) at drain end or empty, A closes sockets, zeroizes STEK ring memory, exits 0. (6) Failure before ACCEPTING: A kills B, unchanged. After ACCEPTING but B crashes: A still holds listener fds and resumes accept loops (rollback window W=10 s). Invariants: UP-1 (queue safety) every listening kernel socket is open in >=1 live process at all times, and no accept queue is ever closed while non-empty without a process polling it. UP-2 (no orphan) after ACK_OWNS no process holds a SO_REUSEPORT listener fd that no accept loop services. UP-3 (graceful stream semantics) every H2 connection of A receives GOAWAY NO_ERROR with last_stream_id >= highest stream it began processing; streams above are un-processed. UP-4 (bounded drain) A exits <= D + epsilon after ACCEPTING; connections open past D are closed and counted (aegis_upgrade_forced_close_total); thus 'no accepted connection dropped before D'. UP-5 (STEK) tickets are encrypted only with a key younger than L_enc and accepted only while key age < L_enc+L_dec (defaults 12h/12h total <=24h); the ring crosses processes only via the handover pipe, never disk; if handover pipe is missing/corrupt B generates a fresh ring (all old tickets fail -> full handshake, never accept-unknown). Key ids unique (128-bit random). A zeroizes on exit. UP-6 (fd hygiene) all non-listener fds CLOEXEC; no fd leaks into helper subprocesses; fd count of A+B <= base + K. UP-7 (config safety) a failing B (config invalid, panic, hang >T_init) never reduces A's service; handover parser returns errors, never panics, caps all lengths. QUIC: out of scope in golden v1 (H3 connections reset on upgrade; clients reconnect) unless CID-routed.
specifics: Crate pins to evaluate: nix 0.31.x (recvmsg, MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC), sd-notify 0.5.0 (notify_with_fds, FdStore), shellflip 2.1.3 only as reference (BSD) - prefer ~300 LOC in-tree; rustls 0.23.46 TicketRotator for the ring semantics or custom ProducesTickets. Model in TLA+ (states: A serving, B starting, B accepting, A draining, A exited; actions incl. crash of either) to check UP-1/UP-2/UP-4.
overclaim_risk: Design synthesized from sources; no implementation run or measured yet. UP-1 in an OS sense depends on kernel behaviour not proven.
underclaim_risk: Strong existence proofs exist for each step individually (HAProxy, Envoy, Pingora, Proxygen).

title: L5: upgrade test harness and CI gate (acceptance criteria for UP-1..UP-7)
summary: Harness (implementation-phase spike; heavy: run only via tools/heavy.sh): loadgen at fixed 2k new conn/s over H1.1, H2 (long streams 5-20 s) and TLS resumption clients; perform 200 consecutive upgrades at 5/s alternating A/B binaries. Pass: 0 connect failures/refused/RST for connections initiated at any time; every in-flight H2 request either completes or sees GOAWAY with last_stream_id below its stream id (client retries successfully); forced-close counter 0 when D > longest stream. Fault injection (deterministic, one per run): SIGKILL B at each protocol step; B hangs before ACCEPTING (A must kill after T_init); invalid config; truncated/oversized handover message; wrong-uid connect to control socket; extra unexpected fd in env; second concurrent upgrade (must be refused). Assert via /proc: fd inventory (no fd without owner, listener fds CLOEXEC in children), `ss -ltn` Recv-Q on listeners never stranded, RSS bounded. STEK check: ring ids/ages logged; test with injected clock that a ticket older than L_enc+L_dec fails to resume and a ticket from before upgrade resumes after (and not after expiry). Fuzz: cargo-fuzz target on handover deserializer (no panics, bounded alloc). Negative controls: run same harness with a naive 'bind second process with SO_REUSEPORT then close' variant and require harness to FAIL it (expect ~2-3 resets/million per HAProxy; may need >=1M conns to observe) to prove oracle power. Gate: harness green on CI nightly; golden release requires 3 consecutive nights.
overclaim_risk: The negative-control loss rate may be unobservable on a small VPS (HAProxy saw errors only when CPU differed from NIC IRQ CPU).
